notes: Seventh sweep (2026-10-31, run head 0814e8d, uncommitted false): five skill runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier. Every transcript reads SKILL.md, the input and references/ex_unit.md with Read, once each, before writing, matching reads in result.json; no Skill tool call. Expected reads (ex_unit.md) is met in 5 of 5. Graded against the previous sweep's grades (sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/log-tests-*.json, at d04061d).

"Group tests by function and name them by behaviour" changed; graded against the current text. The new sentence is "A block named after a condition, or after a requirement where the project asks for that, still states a behaviour a failing test can contradict: `describe "an update survives encoding and applying"`, not `describe "the round trip"`, which names a topic and promises nothing." opus-1 uses describe "charge/3"; haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use "charge/3 when ..." plus a condition; haiku-1 uses condition-only blocks ("when the gateway declines the card", "when the gateway is unavailable", "when the charge succeeds"). None names a topic, so the sentence decides no violation (0 of 5). I read it as forbidding topic names only: the rule's first sentence still endorses `describe "when the subscriber has exited"`, so a "when ..." block that names the situation its tests share is not a topic. If the sentence means a condition block must itself state the outcome, four of five runs would be at issue along with the rule's own example, and the sentence should say so. Test names all name the value returned or what was logged; none has the "returns :ok" shape.

"Run tests concurrently unless they share global state", "Assert with patterns", "Replace dependencies at boundaries, through behaviours" and "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" are unchanged since d04061d and graded to the 2026-10-23 standard; all clean in 5 of 5. All five use async: true with no Logger.configure, Process.register or application env. Assert with patterns: opus-1 and sonnet-1 assert with patterns or the call on the left of ==; haiku-1 puts the call on the left of ==; sonnet-2 binds result = Charger.charge(...) and asserts result == {...} a line later (lines 46-48, 67-69, 87-89), and haiku-2 asserts result == {...} on a result taken from its with_log helper's tuple (lines 28-30, 43-45, 59-61), both the "result bound a line earlier" case the rule's == sentence allows, as sonnet-1 was graded in 2026-10-23; the only bare matches are haiku-2's destructures of the helper's with_log tuple, which cannot fail. Gateways: opus-1 (nested FakeGateway), haiku-1 (Payments.ChargerTest.Gateway) and haiku-2 (Payments.StubGateway) use one behaviour module answering by token; sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use three top-level Payments.ChargerTest.* modules, one per outcome.

Per sentence of the capture_log rule, runs violating: capture_log/2 or with_log/2 rather than a handler, StringIO or backend, 0 of 5; formatter options for format and metadata, 0 of 5 (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 pass :format, :metadata and :colors; opus-1 passes :metadata on the default format in its declined test and only asserts "[error]" in its option-less unavailable capture, which the prompt's error-level check needs); async: true, 0 of 5; wrap every call that logs, 0 of 5 (haiku-1 lines 29, 47, 65, sonnet-1 lines 67, 89 and sonnet-2 lines 45, 66, 86 wrap return-value tests in an option-less capture_log; opus-1 and haiku-2 assert return values inside their log captures); primary-level and crash-report sentences, not exercised in 5 of 5. Success-case absence: opus-1 and sonnet-1 assert an empty level: :warning capture; sonnet-2 asserts an info line and refutes ~r/^(warning|error|critical|alert|emergency)/m; haiku-1 asserts an info line and refutes ~r/^(warning|error) /m; haiku-2 refutes "[warning]" and "[error]". haiku-1 and haiku-2 leave out critical, alert and emergency, as the haiku runs did in 2026-10-23; all met the check.

Outside the case's list, no violation counted. "Build a multi-line argument under a name before the call" changed: it now reads "A keyword list that is the call's last argument stays inline, one option per line", so haiku-2 lines 75-78 and sonnet-1 lines 99-102, where charge/3's trailing options keyword list spans several lines (both written that way by the run, not by the formatter, per the transcripts), are allowed; earlier sweeps counted this shape under the older text. The new "Name a step instead of wrapping an expression": the formatter's wraps after == (haiku-1 lines 30-31, 48-49, 66-67; sonnet-1 47-48, 68-69, 90-91) and after = (sonnet-1 57-58, 76-77, 98-102; sonnet-2 55-56, 76-77, 96-97) hold one comparison of a call with a literal, with no inner step a name would explain beyond `result`, which the rule calls renaming a value used once, so I did not count them. The new fn-body sentence ("one expression stays on the head's line") is not broken: every one-expression fn body passed to capture_log or with_log is too long for the head's line. Not reported, as before: `result` as a variable name (sonnet-2, haiku-2), which ex_unit.md's own `{result, log} = with_log(...)` uses, and opus-1's nested FakeGateway without @moduledoc false in an .exs script that builds no docs. No with, pipeline, capture, case or multi-clause function outside the gateway doubles, whose do: clauses form a table.

Tests were run from copies in the grader scratch folder with elixir -r log-tests-input.ex charger_test.exs on Elixir 1.20.3 (OTP 29), 20 times each with ExUnit's random seed: every file passed every time (opus-1 3 tests; haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 6 each) with no compiler warning and no log line printed. All five pass mix format --check-formatted, confirming format_ok in result.json, and every run checked formatting and ran the tests during the session. As in 2026-10-23, each file was run against five mutants of the input (success logs at warning, declined logs at info, declined drops amount_cents, request_id metadata removed, unavailable logs at warning instead of error): every file fails at least one test on every mutant, so no log assertion is vacuous. opus-1 also wrote its own mutation script to /private/tmp/claude-501/charger-mutants, outside its run folder; it changed no run output.
